reviews.text: The description of this game is inaccurate. The large review sites referencing the good old days of 90's RTSs feel like they never played one. The game is gorgeous. I love the art style and the humour. But the game play is hollow and should not be compared to other RTS games like C&C SC or any others from the 90's because the devs clearly used them more as buzzwords than inspiration. Also, the other reviews on this game seem suspicious AF

Hell, yeah! Finally a proper strategy, not turn-based ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. What makes it stand out from other strategies is its visuals. It's unique. Comical. The game looks like it came out of the pages of a book or a board game. The essence is simple, take control of the territory to produce units and destroy the enemy. +Game is still in early access.
Very fun. You guys need to play this!

《Nuke Them All》相当有趣的小品级RTS，游戏主要以策略决策为主，在并不算大的场地中运筹帷幄，找寻机会占领更多的土地，并出兵击败敌人，基本上游戏没有太多的发育的机会，整个游戏框架十分的轻量级，堪称甜品级的策略性作品。 在玩法上摒弃了复杂的发育机制，完全没有任何资源制约玩家的出兵和发展，无论是开始暴兵还是升级建筑，唯一需要的仅仅是时间，占领更多的资源站点就能获得更多的战争资源，这就是游戏的唯一法则，再此基础上，合理的队伍搭配和操作指挥才是决胜的关键。 而游戏的风格特色也极为休闲恶搞，不仅有那些稀奇古怪的机器人敌人，外星人和丧尸同样是我们需要解决的目标，游戏的整体风格轻松又诙谐，各种角色的动作也极为可爱，整个游戏一共又8个大型章节，不同关卡之间有着鲜明的风格特色，同样还会带来许多意想不到的战斗任务。 游戏着重于塑造各种不同的战场情况供玩家挑战，而并非和大部分的传统RTS一样把重心放在多人对战上，因此本作仅仅适合单人游玩体验。 此外游戏还为玩家提供了作用丰富的的地图编辑器，可以供玩家尽情释放创意，建造一些稀奇古怪的点子。 综合来说作为一款RTS游戏本作确实存在着游戏深度不够、策略性偏弱的问题，但同样的游戏有着十分快的战斗节奏，就像以前的4399小游戏中的RTS，适合闲暇之余体验，而较为搞怪的风格和还算丰富的兵种让游戏又不至于完全不需要思考，喜欢休闲RTS的玩家可以入手一试。 [quote] 游玩百态，将游玩心得用汉语化作玩家的指明灯，(๑•̀ㅂ•́)و✧ [url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/35402408/]点击这里关注汉化语录~[/url] 如果喜欢这个评测，请点个赞让更多人看见 [/quote]

Nuke Them All is an addictive arcade game that provides addictive gameplay. In this game, you have to protect the world from the invasion of evil aliens. The endless waves of enemies ensure that the game is truly addictive and never lets you get bored. The graphics and soundtrack also deserve praise. Each level is made with attention to detail. Easy to master thanks to intuitive controls and simple game mechanics.

This is a fun casual real-time strategy game in the atmosphere of the classic RTS Z (1996) and Z: Steel Soldiers (2001). The graphics in the game resemble an interactive cartoon. There is no tedious, boring process of building a base and collecting resources. You capture territories, improve buildings, unlock new technologies and weapons to create a powerful army and defeat your enemies. Nuke Them All The will appeal to both children and adults. There is a lot of humor and funny cutscenes; there are various missions, a sandbox mode and even a game of football!

Takes too long for units to get manufactured and just feels like a war for attrition most of the time (with the AI) and most of the time it just feels unfair and that coupled with the lack of optimization even on Potato settings due to the engine only allowing 60FPS max. And don't bother attempting to turn off V-Sync options in your AMD/Nvidia Software/Panel because it just adds screen tearing without the benefits of framerate gaining. Because there is nothing past 60FPS. Honestly I've never felt like I've wasted money on a game before but this game? Feels like an "F you" to the consumer. The developer is also dead silent in the community forums on Steam so don't expect any help or assistance from the developers. And it's a shame because the artstyle and gameplay could be better.

CONCLUSION Graphics: 8/10 cartoonish but fun Sound: 5/10 Music 10/10 - epic soundtracks from 90x Gameplay 8/10 very chaotic but strategical "Nuke Them All" combines the best of classic RTS games with modern humor. The cutscenes are filled with dad jokes and puns that add a fun, lighthearted touch. The missions are diverse and challenging, making it a great choice for fans of the genre.

Absolutely love this game! It's like stepping back into the 90s with "Z," but with a fresh, modern twist. The graphics are fantastic, capturing a unique, comical style that makes the gameplay enjoyable. There are over 20 missions, each with different scenarios and stories. The "Doomsday Clock" mission explaining the origins of the story is a standout. The new units like Rage Balloon and Air Ship add a lot of fun, and the Nuke Football mode is hilarious. Occasional bugs, but nothing game-breaking. Highly recommended for RTS fans!

okay! The concept is great, bringing back memories of classic RTS games, but the execution falls short. The controls are clunky, and the AI is often unresponsive. The humor feels forced, and the overall gameplay lacks depth. The graphics are nice, but it doesn't make up for the shallow experience. It needs more polish and bug fixes to be truly enjoyable. For now, it feels more like a mobile game than a serious RTS. Hopefully, future updates will address these issues.

It's ok with discount! "Nuke Them All" isn't an AAA title, but it's a commendable effort for a solo indie developer. The concept is intriguing, and the base-building and crystal collection mechanics add depth. The map editor is a nice touch, allowing creativity and customization. However, the game falls short in several areas. The controls feel clunky, and the AI is often unresponsive. The humor can be hit or miss. Still good enough for a solo dev.

This game brilliantly captures the charm of old Bitmap Brothers' "Z" with its unique art style and engaging gameplay. The dad jokes and puns in the cutscenes are a delightful touch, adding a layer of humor that keeps the game entertaining. A must-play for fans of classic RTS games!

Pros: Unique and engaging missions Fun new units like Rage Balloon and Air Ship Entertaining humor and cutscenes Cons: Some bugs but no crashes AI can be unpredictable and chaotic Graphics: 8/10 Sound: 7/10 A great blend of nostalgia and modern twists, capturing the essence of classic RTS games with fresh elements.

Recommended This game rocks! It brings back the good old RTS vibes from the 90s. The missions are fun and challenging, although there are some bugs. The unique units and engaging storylines keep things interesting. Plus, the graphics and cutscenes add a nice touch of humor. Definitely worth a try for any RTS fan.

Good with a discount. VERY fast paced! I enjoyed the improved sandbox mode and the new units like the Headbot, Mech General Zod. The base-building and resource collection mechanics add depth, and the technology tree provides a sense of progression. The game's humor, coupled with the dad jokes in cutscenes, makes it entertaining.

Loving the art style, feels like clash royale! It’s like stepping back into the 90s with "Z," but with a fresh, modern twist. The graphics are fantastic, capturing a unique, comical style that makes the gameplay enjoyable. There are over 20 missions, each with different scenarios and stories. Occasional bugs, but nothing game-breaking. Highly recommended for RTS fans!

New cutscenes with dad jokes bring back Z vibes! As a long-time fan of RTS games, I found "Nuke Them All" to be a refreshing take on the genre. The game stands out with its unique art style and engaging story missions. The ability to control the nuclear bomb with the space bar and arrow keys adds an exciting dynamic. I also appreciated the addition of base-building and resource collection, which adds a layer of strategy. The game includes a variety of modes, from Nuke Football to zombie survival challenges. While there are occasional bugs, the overall experience is fun and nostalgic.

This game is a delightful mix of nostalgia and new features. It successfully captures the essence of classic RTS games while introducing modern elements like nukes. The tutorial is quick and easy, making it accessible even for new players. I love the zombie survival and tower defense elements on some maps, especially the Death Canyon. The simple map editor is a fantastic addition, allowing players to create and share their own maps. While it has a few bugs, the engaging missions and unique units make it worth playing.

"Nuke Them All" is a fun, casual RTS that offers a unique twist on classic gameplay. The game features over 20 missions with different scenarios, including the epic "Doomsday Clock" mission. I enjoyed the improved sandbox mode and the new units like the Headbot Backpacker, Drone operator and General Zod. The base-building and resource collection mechanics add depth, and the technology tree provides a sense of progression. The game's humor, coupled with the dad jokes in cutscenes, makes it entertaining. Despite a few balancing issues, it's a solid game for RTS enthusiasts.

Nuke them all is a fantastic game that keeps me entertained for hours. The graphics are amazing and the gameplay is addictive. I love the variety of levels and challenges that keep me coming back for more. I highly recommend this game to anyone looking for a fun and exciting gaming experience.

首先感谢作者和发行大佬们对UU鉴赏家的信任，赠送了一份珍贵作品的牵线副本。 如此“厚礼”，不知要如何表达感谢，不如就赠上一篇简中语言区的好评吧！ 至于内容好与不好，看官姥爷们可参考以下正文内容，再考虑是否支持该作品！ [h1][quote=] [table] [tr] [th] 欢迎关注 [url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/38287879]网易UU鉴赏家培养计划[/url][/th] [/tr] [tr] [th] 关注UU加速器VX公众号，回复“steam”，获得专属玩家群邀请。 [/th] [/tr] [/table] [/quote][/h1] 《Nuke Them All》是一款玩法较为简单的RTS作品。 何为简单？一般来说，即时战略都需要有扩张、发展、生产以及战斗等各个因素组成。而它是非常纯粹的战斗玩法，以关卡的形式、简单的红蓝双方对抗，并不需要有建造和采集资源等内容，上手直接就是战术指挥战斗的RTS。自己家建筑的来源在于争夺、占领而“转化”得来，升级科技亦是同理，至于生产是建筑自行运行而非玩家去干预生产队列。 本作由Indie PapaMike开发制作，由GameEraStudios担任发行工作。是一款较早发布EA测试，今年6月刚刚迎来正式版的作品。可惜，仍无中文支持。 它所谓的简单，不仅在于其玩法的简化，还在于它的桌布。 游戏的场景各式各样，但是若要一一去做一种精致的地形地图，不仅制作难度会提升，优化也可能会由问题。因此制作组有了一种很巧妙的方式解决了背景问题，那就是用一种平面的背景图当作背景，在背景图上放置上可交互的建筑模型与可操作的军队模型，便成了对抗战场。真是物理层面上的“纸上谈兵”呀！ 而作为策略游戏，其操作方式与其他作品是大同小异的，左键选取，右键交互移动，只要是RTS老玩家，上手几乎没有难度。就算是新人也好，游戏的教程非常完整，甚至还录制了真人影像，在教学过程中实时解说。还是那句话，可惜没有中文的支持，甚至没有字幕，这将会是大多数国人比较高的游玩门槛。
难能可贵的即时战略游戏，卡通风格。 即时战略鲜有人做，尤为珍贵，且玩且珍惜！推荐！

So you want to know about Nuke Them All. Sit down son. I will tell you everything you need to know why you should [b]ABSOLUTELY NOT[/b] buy this definitely still early access title. And make no mistake the positive ones are probably trolls or paid off. There is nothing worthy of awards to this game. Let's Begin. But first for those score inclined: [b]2.5/10[/b] this is graded down from it's original 25/100 and 25 is generous. My journey begun when I received a free review copy. Only requirement: Play the game, "We are doing a content and you might win money." Bad start. Let's move on. I streamed the game and behold it launches. [h1] Options: 1/10[/h1] First thing I do is head over to the options to customise my experience, after all I am a pc user. Graphics are : Windowed or Full Screen... Sound: Pick between bar 1,2,3,4 Change controls? Absolutely not. Does it remember to put the game in windowed mode? Absolutely.... As long as you remember to enter settings every time. Ooofff very bad start. Smells like a ♥♥♥♥ mobile game. [h1] Tutorial: 0/10[/h1] I click on the first map available. FORCED TUTORIAL.... Great... I think to myself. Oh look. The tutorial tells you to do things. And is the ONLY time you are told the controls. Hope you screenshot them. Or you can remember at all times what they were from memory. You play through an interactive tutorial which is an interesting idea however the voice over never repeats herself and no there are no subtitles or visible goals. The greatest thing about the tutorial is that it's short. [h1] Gameplay: 4/10[/h1] The game is simple. You start with a fortress, destroy the opponent fortress. No matter what you do, they are stronger produce units practically without factories and will start with overwhelming force in most cases. That's right, ♥♥♥♥ balance. Give the enemy overwhelming force right out the gate, high tier units attempting to grab your factories from 1st second of gameplay. The only way you will win is by taking factories and depriving the opponent of theirs. The easiest way to do this is simply by obtaining and holding the nuke, then erasing their factories. It's fun-ish, but random events will constantly hassle you and kill mostly YOUR units as they almost always seem to hit JUST YOUR UNITS and magically avoid enemy troops. Not to say they can't, They just mostly don't. The game tells you to cap flags as they "increase your production speed." in fact the first thing taught to you in the tutorial. Unfortunately this is a simple lie, they do ♥♥♥♥ all. Sorry. Their purpose is to set alignment of nearby buildings. Cap factories, upgrade where possible without disrupting your supply lines and you'll maybe be fine. If you want a FAR better gameplay of this type of rts where you have no resources to worry about. Go play "State of War" a game released in 2001 and FAR superior to this questionable money grab. Techtree exists... It's cross map and it's actual use seems incomprehensible as the enemy can upgrade building beyond your tech level and as soon as you take the flag you claim their factories. So... What is the point of this? So you can do the upgrades yourself. Remember, it only takes one unit, 2 seconds of being near the flag. To capture the factory. Most factories take 30+ seconds to produce. Rush when they send an army and you won't have any trouble stealing it. [h1] Stability: 3/10[/h1] The game crashes at least once per map. Steam achievement? Crash. Send a unit in a way it doesn't like? Crash. Changed an option it didn't like? Crash. Opened map editor? Crash. Tried to load your edited map before the controls menu pops up? Guaran-♥♥♥♥♥♥♥-teed my dude, crash my man. Played the game once before ever? Enjoy getting a popup every time asking you if you want to load quick save. Oh hohoho you wanted to load your game? Crash. [h1] The Map Editor: -5/10 THESE GO NEGATIVE? ♥♥♥♥ yes I am making an exception for this one.[/h1] The developers couldn't be bothered making a map editor so what you get is an active scenario. You can't drag units that aren't yours. And can't drag units that aren't moveable buildings. You can't delete things unless you drag them into the deletion button. But if I can't move them.... Then how do I delete them? You don't. You can move the base structures? Yes. Once. Then they are immovable objects that will never meet an unstoppable force. There is no scripting. Despite the developer making it looks that way by putting their image of custom maps as a STANDARD map from the main campaign. There are many hotkeys which spawn varieties of things but devs never bothered writing them down or creating an F1 help menu to help you understand ANYTHING about their editor. Oh and units shoot at each other WHILE the editor is paused ofcourse... [h1] Variety: 2/10[/h1] [list] [*]6 maps on the desert world [*]3 jungle world [*]3 zombieland [*]3 volcano world [*]3 ice world [*]3 space world [*]3 wasteland [/list] 24 maps and they aren't bad. Some are gimmicks. Like "Nuke Ball" which is also the "proud creation" of the unusable map editor according to their store page. You know that map editor with no scripting support. M O V I N G ON [h1] Cutscenes; 4/10[/h1] I'ma give the game a break now. And talk about it's cutscene. These happen outside of the gameplay look thankfully. And atleast are ACTUALLY humorous. However I do not recommend buying a game for just it's funny weird cutscenes. I've only seen 3 and one of those was the intro when booting the game. Other are desert world and ice world. [h1] Animation: 10/10[/h1] The animations in-game and in-videos are very nice. A lot of love was put into it. [h1] GUI: 0/10[/h1] What gui? Designed by DJ Khaled. Clearly. [h1] Music: 6/10[/h1] The music is nice, enjoy listening to the same track for practically all 1 hours you can stomach. Juding by all other reviewers seeeming to have at max about 1 hour give or take. [h1] Final commentary:[/h1] While the game is playable, at max you'd be playing it for 4 hours, completed all there is to do and throw it in the bin. The game presents itself nicely with nice graphics and sounds. But programming was clearly done by a 3 year old using chat gpt. From the weird arch based pathing instead of A* to the constant crashes. Auto saves mere seconds after reloading from a crash. Bad gui, and generally half the time units refusing to follow simple orders. This game is let down in every way humanly possible by the blatant lack of testing. The fact this game was allowed to actually release in order to pretend not to be an "Early Access" title is revolting. The fact the game credits as me to whishlist on steam is even more revolting. Because it indicates to me this is probably the demo with the word demo removed. It quotes " Z (1996), as well as modern classics like Company of Heroes, and They Are Billions.." as being games it is like. Go play those games, they are unlike this... Actually worth your money. [i]M A K E NO M I S T A K E.[/i] This game IS [i]ABSOLUTELY 100%[/i] uncooked. You're eating raw tonight. I hope in the future I can revise this and see the cash grab turn into an actual game worth my time. As it stands. I spend more than the game's worth of time "playing" it. So you never have to. If I had my name to this as a programmer i'd ask to have my name removed out of shame.

RTS is my genre. This is not RTS. They cut out virtually everything that separates an RTS from a tactics or a randomly assorted mobile game. There is no base building or resource management. There is barely defense placement. There are no macro choices, the factories on the map can be taken or destroyed/repaired, you don't choose which structures or units to build or when. The game is ENTIRELY: drag-select a group of units, attack-move them to a defensive choke point or forwards into the enemy. Occasionally target an ability, like a Nuke. That's the entire game play loop; that's all you ever do. It's indie, I don't want to be too harsh, but they're abusing my #1 genre's tag. This IS NOT RTS. Get these imposters the hell out of my genre. Buy this for your 3-year-old nephew, he'll like it for all of 30 minutes. ... and it's pretty damn buggy. There's almost nothing going on here and it's all sloppy (poor collision, messy pathing, attack-scan hang-ups). I've got freezes and occasionally "FPS drop detected, resetting..." then the whole game jumps back 5 seconds and random units die.

I went into Nuke Them All expecting a decent retro RTS but came out absolutely hooked. This game gets so many things right: the fast-paced flag captures, the way enemies adapt to your tactics, and the glorious feel of unleashing a nuke at the perfect moment. Even better, there’s a night mode where zombies come at you like clockwork, making you rethink your plans on the fly. The art style is an amazing throwback to the 90s without looking outdated. This game has done something special for RTS fans who crave that old-school chaos with just enough newness to keep it fresh.

Enjoyable gameplay with some cool mechanics, but it does feel a bit repetitive after a while. The graphics aren’t my favorite, but the humor and unique unit types make it an interesting experience. Worth picking up if you love RTS games.

This is not one of those RTS games where you’re drowning in menus or clicking a million things—Nuke Them All lets you focus on the fun stuff: strategy, big moves, and pure mayhem. Can’t believe it’s an indie title; it’s incredibly well-crafted and perfectly balanced between simplicity and depth.

While Nuke Them All has an engaging pace, the visuals lack polish. The strategy is good and the humor adds personality, but it’s not the prettiest game out there. Still, for fans of old-school RTS, it has a lot of charm.

Nuke Them All is a hidden gem for RTS fans who don’t need AAA graphics to have a great time. The gameplay is straightforward but engaging, focusing on capturing flags and outmaneuvering enemies, which gives it a refreshing simplicity. The humor is a nice touch, adding personality and charm. The visuals are pretty basic, but it has a nostalgic, retro charm for anyone who enjoyed classic 90s games. If you’re looking for something fun, strategic, and unique, this is absolutely worth a try.

Gotta say, the gameplay is super engaging, and the humor gives it a unique charm that keeps me coming back. Every session feels fresh with those unpredictable moments and crazy enemy waves. Visually, it leans a bit too retro for my taste, but if you’re in it for the mechanics and personality, it’s a solid game that doesn’t disappoint!

The humor is absolutely on point - love the quirky one-liners from the units, which give it a charm you don’t often see. The gameplay is fast-paced and strategic, a welcome change from endless micromanagement. That said, the graphics aren’t the game’s strong suit. They have that retro look, which fits, but it may not be for everyone. Still, the gameplay more than makes up for it.

As someone who’s not into endless micromanaging, Nuke Them All is an absolute blast. It’s pure strategy without the headache, perfect for a quick adrenaline rush. I got lost in it for hours without even realizing—this is classic RTS done right!

Fun concept, but the graphics feel outdated even for a retro game. The gameplay is solid and fast-paced, though, so if you can look past the visuals, it’s worth a try. Good option for a quick RTS fix.
